I’m narrowing whether the sandbox profile omitted harmless ancestor-path metadata reads or whether Ruby 4/macOS 26 introduced a broader requirement.

content.text:
The discussion reports a real mise bug, not missing setup.

I reproduced it on macOS 26.6.2 with mise’s precompiled Ruby 4.0.6:

- Current sandbox profile: Ruby exits with `rb_check_realpath_internal` / `EPERM`.
- Add `(allow file-read-metadata (literal "/private"))`: Ruby starts successfully.
- Ruby never reaches the tap formula, so this is unrelated to `alerter`, Homebrew activation, or the formula contents.

Cause: mise’s portable Ruby is built with `--enable-load-relative`, which resolves its executable path during startup. The sandbox permits reading `/private/tmp/**`, but denies metadata access to its parent `/private`. The existing root exception grants only `file-read-data`, not the required metadata access. The affected sandbox is used by both formula and cask evaluation in [tap.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/f8c1/mise/src/system/packages/brew/tap.rs:58), while the missing rule is in [macos.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/f8c1/mise/src/sandbox/macos.rs:51).

The narrow fix is to permit metadata—not file contents or directory enumeration—on literal `/private` in read-restricted macOS profiles. A regression test should verify:

- metadata lookup on `/private` succeeds;
- reading or listing unauthorized descendants remains blocked;
- portable Ruby can start inside the metadata sandbox.

This is closely related to the earlier [root traversal fix in PR #12263](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/12263), but that fix covered root data access rather than `/private` metadata. The reporter’s diagnosis in [Discussion #12937](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/12937) is therefore essentially correct.

No repository files were changed, and the temporary isolated Ruby installation was removed.
make a pr, post a reply

I’ll implement the narrow `/private` metadata exception with a runtime regression test that also proves directory contents remain unreadable, run the focused checks, then commit, open a review-ready PR, and reply to the discussion with the diagnosis and PR link.

 cmd:`git push -u origin codex/fix-macos-private-metadata
gh pr create --repo jdx/mise --base main --head codex/fix-macos-private-metadata --title 'fix(sandbox): allow metadata access to macOS private directory' --body '## Summary

- allow metadata access to the literal \`/private\` directory in read-restricted macOS Seatbelt profiles
- preserve denial of directory listings and descendant reads
- document the narrow implicit permission

## Context
